αἰθούσῃ: αἴθουσα — portico, colonnaded hall; fem. dat. sg.
αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον)
αἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj., epic/dialectal by-form αἰ (used before κε)
αἴης: αἶα — land, earth; gen. sg., epic by-form of γαῖα
αἶψ: αἶψα — quickly, swiftly; adv., elided (αἶψ’ = αἶψα)
αὐτίκ: αὐτίκα (elided αὐτίκ’) — at once, immediately, forthwith; adv.
αὐτόν: αὐτός — self; masc. acc. sg.: ’himself’, or reinforcing a pronoun of any person (με … καὶ αὐτόν ’me myself as well’)
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.
βάλε: βάλλω — throw, cast; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔβαλε): ’cast’
βουλήν: βουλή — plan, counsel, decision; acc. sg.
βοὴν: βοή — shout, war-cry; fem. acc. sg. of respect: ‘good at the war-cry’ (βοὴν ἀγαθός)
βοῦς: βοῦς — ox, cow; pl. ’cattle’; acc. pl. · also masc./fem. nom. sg. (same spelling as the acc. pl.): ’the ox, the heifer’ (ἦλθε ... βοῦς ’the heifer came’)
βῆ: βαίνω — go, walk, step; aor. 3 sg., root aorist, unaugmented (= ἔβη): ’went, strode’
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γούναθ: γόνυ (pl. γούνατα) — knee; neut. acc. pl., elided and aspirated (γούναθ’ = γούνατα); clasping the knees is the suppliant’s gesture
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive with δῖα: ’heavenly-one of women’
γύναι: γυνή — woman, wife; fem. voc. sg.: ’wife’
δάκρυ: δάκρυ — tear; neut. acc. sg., used collectively: ’tears’ · also elided δάκρυ’ = δάκρυα, neut. acc. pl.
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δήμιον: δήμιος — of the δῆμος, public; neut. acc. sg. (δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’)
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δαίμων: δαίμων — a god, some divine power (vague, unspecified); masc. nom. sg.
δαναῶν: Δαναοί — the Danaans, the Greeks; masc. gen. pl.
δεῦρ: δεῦρο — hither, here; adv., elided (δεῦρ’ = δεῦρο)
διοτρεφές: διοτρεφής — Zeus-nurtured (epithet of kings); adj., masc. voc. sg.
δυσμενέων: δυσμενέω — be hostile, bear ill will; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic δυσμενῶν)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
δῖαν: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. acc. sg. δῖαν, here extended to the sea (ἅλα δῖαν ’the heavenly brine’) rather than a hero · also of a place-name: Λακεδαίμονα δῖαν ’heavenly Lacedaemon’
δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)
εἰλίποδας: εἰλίπους — rolling-gaited, swaying-footed (of cattle); masc./fem. acc. pl.
εἰς: εἰς — into, to; prep. + acc. · also εἰμί ’be’: pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ): ’you are’ (τίς … εἰς; ’who are you?’)
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’)
εἵματα: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl.
εἶδος: εἶδος — form, look, beauty; neut. acc. sg. (accusative of respect): ’in beauty’
εὐνῆφι: εὐνή — bed; sg. with the epic case-ending -φι(ν), serving as gen. or dat. (ἐξ εὐνῆφι ’out of bed’; = Attic ἐξ εὐνῆς)
εὐρέα: εὐρύς — wide, broad; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα ’broad backs’ (ἐπ’ εὐρέα νῶτα θαλάσσης ’over the broad back of the sea’)
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θέτ: τίθημι — put, place, set; aor. mid. 3 sg., unaugmented, elided (θέτ’ = θέτο), in tmesis (περὶ … θέτ’ = περιέθετο): ’set about’
θαλάμοιο: θάλαμος — chamber, room; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’)
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κάκ: κακός — bad, evil; neut. acc. pl. (elided κάκ’): ’evils, misfortunes’
καθεῦδε: καθεύδω — sleep, lie down to sleep; impf. 3 sg., no augment shown (Attic καθηῦδε or ἐκάθευδε; Attic too often leaves εὐ- unchanged)
καλὰ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; neut. acc. pl.
κατάλεξον: καταλέγω — recount in full and in order (not yet ’choose’, as later); aor. imper. 2 sg.
κατέρυκε: κατερύκω — hold back, detain; pres. imper. 2 sg. (with μή: ’stop holding back’) · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic κατήρυκε): ’was holding back, tried to hold back’
καταλέξω: καταλέγω — recount in full and in order; fut. 1 sg. or aor. subj. 1 sg. (the epic forms coincide): ’I will tell in full’
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
κείνου: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. gen. sg.
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κεῖσε: κεῖσε — to that place, thither; adv.
κτείνας: κτείνω — kill, slay; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ‘having killed’
κῆρ: κῆρ — heart; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect (φίλον κῆρ ’in his own heart’)
κῆρα: κήρ — doom, fate of death; fem. acc. sg.
κῦδος: κῦδος — glory, the lustre of success granted by a god; neut. nom./acc. sg.
λίσσομαι: λίσσομαι — beseech, entreat; pres. 1 sg., + gen. of the power invoked · also + acc. of the person entreated (and acc. of the thing asked): οὐχ ὑμέας ἔτι λίσσομαι ’I no longer beg you’ · also used absolutely, the addressee already given by context and left unexpressed, with the ground of the appeal in a following clause (λίσσομαι, εἴ ποτέ ...)
λακεδαίμονα: Λακεδαίμων — Lacedaemon, the land in which Sparta lies; fem. acc. sg.
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’)
λιπαροῖσιν: λιπαρός — sleek, glistening, glossy (as skin rubbed with oil); masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οῖς)
λυγρά: λυγρός — grievous, baneful, miserable; adj., neut. acc. pl.: ‘grievous things’
λυγρὸν: λυγρός — baneful, bitter, grievous; masc. acc. sg.
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’
μεγάροιο: μέγαρον — hall; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
μεγάροισι: μέγαρον — hall; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
μειλίσσεο: μειλίσσω — soothe, make mild, soften; pres. imper. mid. 2 sg., uncontracted (= Attic μειλίσσου)
μενέλαε: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta; masc. voc. sg.
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’)
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’)
μηδ: μηδέ — and not, nor; neg. conj., elided (μηδ’ = μηδέ)
μηδέ: μηδέ — and not, nor, do not; neg. conj., used to forbid before an imperative
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μνῆσαι: μιμνήσκω — remind; mid. remember, be mindful; aor. imper. mid. 2 sg.: ’remember!’
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μοῖραν: μοῖρα — due share, what is fitting, portion, fate; fem. acc. sg. (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’)
μυχῷ: μυχός — innermost part, corner, recess; masc. dat. sg.
μύθοισιν: μῦθος — word, speech; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses
μῆλ: μῆλον — sheep or goat, flock-animal; neut. acc. pl. (elided μῆλ’)
μῦθον: μῦθος — word, speech, thing said; acc. sg.
νέεσθαι: νέομαι — go, return home; pres. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic νεῖσθαι)
νημερτὲς: νημερτής — unerring, infallible; neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’the unerring truth’
νηυσὶν: ναῦς — ship; fem. dat. pl., epic νηυσί(ν)
νόσφιν: νόσφιν — apart, far off, away; adv.
νῆάς: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
νῶι: ἐγώ (dual νῶι) — we two; acc. dual: ’the two of us’ (μετὰ νῶι ’after the two of us’)  ·  also used as nom. dual: νῶι … ἱκόμεθ’ ’we two have come’
νῶτα: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. pl. νῶτα, poetic image ’the broad back(s) of the sea’
ξανθὸς: ξανθός — fair-haired, yellow, tawny; masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Menelaus
ξείνους: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); masc. acc. pl.

οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἵδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’these here’
οἶος: οἶος — alone, only; masc. nom. sg.

οὐδὲν: οὐδείς, οὐδεμία, οὐδέν — no one, nothing; neut. acc./nom. sg. used adverbially: ’not at all’
οὐκ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., form before a vowel with smooth breathing (οὐχ before a rough breathing)

οὔλας: οὖλος — thick, woolly, curly; fem. acc. pl.
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.

πάντες: πᾶς — all, every; masc. nom. pl.
πάσχετε: πάσχω — suffer, experience; impf. 2 pl., unaugmented (= ἐπάσχετε)
πήματ: πῆμα — woe, suffering, calamity; neut. acc. pl., elided (πήματ’ = πήματα)
πίονα: πίων — fat, rich; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα: ’fat’
παλλὰς: Παλλάς — Pallas, title of Athena of unknown origin (perhaps πάλλω ’brandish’); nom. sg.
παράκοιτις: παράκοιτις — bedfellow, wife; fem. nom. sg.
πατρίδος: πατρίς — fatherland, native land; gen. sg.
παῖδες: παῖς — child, son; masc. nom. pl.

πλεῖστα: πολύς — much, many; superlative πλεῖστος, neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’most, the greatest amount’
πολλοὺς: πολύς — much, many; masc. acc. pl.
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’
πολλὴν: πολύς — much, many; fem. acc. sg.
ποσσὶ: πούς — foot; masc. dat. pl., epic ποσσί (= Attic ποσί)
ποτέ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; encl. adv.
πρίν: πρίν — before, until; conj./adv., + inf. πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf.
πω: πω — yet, up to now; enclitic adv., usu. with a negative
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)

σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’

σφάζουσι: σφάζω — slaughter, slay (esp. for sacrifice); pres. 3 pl.
σὰ: σός — your (sg.); neut. acc. pl., agreeing with a neut. pl. noun: ’your (knees)’
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)

τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)

τέ: τε — and; enclitic connective, also marks a standing fact (epic τε)
τέκε: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., no augment (= ἔτεκε)

τίπτε: τίπτε — why ever, what then (= τί ποτε shortened); interrog. adv.
ταλασίφρονος: ταλασίφρων — enduring-minded, steadfast; gen. sg. (epithet of Odysseus, from τλῆναι ’endure’)
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τεοῖσιν: τεός (epic possessive = σός) — your, yours; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic σοῖς)
τευ: τις, τι — someone, something; indefinite pron., masc./fem. gen. sg., epic τευ (= Attic τινός)
τηλέμαχ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. voc. sg., elided (Τηλέμαχ’ = Τηλέμαχε)
τηλέμαχος: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; nom. sg.
τηλέμαχός: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. nom. sg. (accented before enclitic θ’)
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.

τινά: τις, τι — someone, something; masc. acc. sg., indefinite, accented before enclitic οἱ (with ὅν: ὅν τινα ’whatever’)
τοί: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. pl. ’they’ · also relative: ’who’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιοῦτον: τοιοῦτος — such, of this kind; masc. acc. sg.
τοὔνεκα: τοὔνεκα (crasis of τοῦ ἕνεκα) — for this reason, therefore; adv.
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj.
τοῖος: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; masc. nom. sg. (τοῖος ... οἷον ’such as’)
τρὶς: τρίς — three times, thrice; numeral adv.
τόδ: ὅδε — this, this here; neut. nom./acc. sg., elided (τόδ’ = τόδε)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τόφρα: τόφρα — so long, meanwhile; adv., correlative with ἕως ’until’
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’)
υἷες: υἱός — son; masc. nom. pl., epic υἷες (= Attic υἱεῖς)
φάνη: φαίνω — show; aor. pass. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐφάνη): ’appeared’
φάρμακον: φάρμακον — drug, potion (healing or deadly); acc. sg.
φέροντες: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
φίλης: φίλος — dear, one’s own; fem. gen. sg.

φρένας: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. acc. pl.
φρόνιν: φρόνις — wisdom, prudence, understanding; fem. acc. sg. (rare poetic noun)
φωτὶ: φώς — man, mortal; masc. dat. sg.
φόνον: φόνος — murder, slaughter, bloodshed; masc. acc. sg.
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χλαίνας: χλαῖνα — a thick cloak, mantle; fem. acc. pl.
χρειὼ: χρειώ — need, want, business; fem. nom. sg., epic by-form of χρεία; in τίνα χρειὼ … ἵκει ’whom has need come upon?’
ἀγαθὸς: ἀγαθός — good, brave, noble; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἀγλαὸς: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant; masc. nom. sg.
ἀδελφεὸν: ἀδελφεός — brother (epic form = Attic ἀδελφός); masc. acc. sg.
ἀθήνη: Ἀθήνη — Athena, goddess of wisdom and war; nom. sg.
ἀμείψασθαι: ἀμείβομαι — answer, reply, exchange (words); aor. inf. mid.
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’)
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv.
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; gen. pl.
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀρίστους: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος, masc. acc. pl.: ’best’
ἀργείη: Ἀργεῖος — Argive; adj., fem. nom. sg.
ἀργείων: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀτρεΐδη: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus; masc. voc. sg.
ἀτρεΐδης: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
ἀτὰρ: ἀτάρ — but, and; epic conj. (by-form of αὐτάρ)
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχαιούς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. acc. pl.
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἁδινὰ: ἁδινός — close-packed, thronging, in a mass; neut. acc. pl.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἂρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, grave form ἂρ (ἐπεὶ ἂρ δή ’since, as it seems’)
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg.
ἄκουσας: ἀκούω — hear; aor. 2 sg., unaugmented (= ἤκουσας), + gen. of source
ἄλλ: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. acc. sg., elided (ἄλλ’ = ἄλλο): ’another thing’
ἄλλαι: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. nom. pl.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄλλοτε: ἄλλοτε — at another time, at one time … at another; adv.
ἄλλῳ: ἄλλος — other, another; masc./neut. dat. sg.
ἄντην: ἄντην — face to face, to the eye, in front; adv.
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel
ἄριστοι: ἄριστος — best; superl., masc. nom. pl.
ἄρουρα: ἄρουρα — ploughland, soil; fem. nom. sg.
ἅπαντα: ἅπας — all, the whole of; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom./acc. pl., subject or object of a verb: ’all things’ (τελευτηθῆναι ἅπαντα ’that all things were fulfilled’)
ἐγὼν: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg., form used before a vowel
ἐδήσατο: δέω — bind; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’bound on (for herself)’
ἐθέλῃσθα: ἐθέλω — be willing, wish; pres. subj. 2 sg., epic ending -ῃσθα (= Attic ἐθέλῃς)
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκγεγαυῖα: ἐκγίγνομαι — be sprung from, be born of; perf. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’sprung (from)’
ἐλαίῳ: ἔλαιον — olive oil; neut. dat. sg.
ἐλεαίρων: ἐλεαίρω (epic by-form of ἐλεέω) — pity, have compassion on; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.
ἐμός: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. nom. sg.
ἐμὴν: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. acc. sg.
ἐμὸν: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἐμῆς: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. gen. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνίσπες: ἐνέπω/ἐνίσπω — tell, relate, declare; aor. imper. 2 sg.: ’tell!’
ἐναλίγκιος: ἐναλίγκιος — like, resembling (+ dat.); masc. nom. sg.
ἐνισπεῖν: ἐνέπω/ἐνίσπω — tell, relate, declare; aor. inf.: ’to tell’
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐξαῦτις: ἐξαῦτις — again, once more, anew; adv., epic (= Attic αὖθις)
ἐξετέλεσσε: ἐκτελέω — bring to completion, finish; aor. 3 sg.
ἐοικότα: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting; perf. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’fitting’ (ἐοικότα μυθήσασθαι ’to speak fittingly’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέεσσιν: ἔπος — word; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν)
ἐπὴν: ἐπήν — when, whenever (= ἐπεὶ ἄν); conj. + subj.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλά: ἐσθλός — good, noble, excellent; neut. acc. pl.
ἐσθλὰ: ἐσθλός — good, noble, staunch; neut. acc. pl.
ἐσθλὸς: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. nom. sg.
ἐόντα: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc./neut. acc. sg., epic (= Attic ὄντα)
ἑλένη: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. nom. sg.
ἑσσάμενος: ἕννυμι — clothe, put on; aor. part. masc. nom. sg. mid.: ’having put on (for himself)’
ἔειπες: εἶπον — say, speak; aor. 2 sg., epic uncontracted, augment ἐ- kept (ἔειπες = εἶπες)
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen., placed after its pronoun with anastrophe: τοῦ ... ἔκ = ἐκ τοῦ ’from him’ · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε ’called by name’)
ἔνδοθεν: ἔνδοθεν — from within, within; adv., -θεν suffix of place
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθεν: ἔνθεν — from there, thence; adv. of place, with suffix -θεν
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with anastrophe, accent thrown back after its noun (δήμῳ ἔνι = ἐν δήμῳ)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl.
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’)
ἔσαν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἦσαν)
ἔτλη: τλάω — bring oneself to, dare, endure; aor. 3 sg. (ἔτλην, inf. τλῆναι)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχε: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic εἶχε)
ἔχοντες: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἕκαστος: ἕκαστος — each, every; masc. nom. sg.
ἕλικας: ἕλιξ — twisted, curved (of cattle’s horns); fem. acc. pl.
ἠέ: ἠέ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic = ἤ), esp. in ἠέ ... ἦ ’either... or’
ἠριγένεια: ἠριγένεια — early-born; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ἠώς: ἠώς — dawn; fem. nom. sg. (personified Ἠώς, Attic Ἕως)
ἡμέας: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; acc. pl., epic ἡμέας (= Attic ἡμᾶς)
ἣν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. acc. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which (fem. acc. sg.)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤντησας: ἀντάω — meet with, encounter; aor. 2 sg., augmented, + gen.: ’you came upon’
ἥμενοι: ἧμαι — sit; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.
ἥρως: ἥρως — hero, man of standing; masc. nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἦμος: ἦμος — when, at the time when; temporal conj.
ἱκάνομαι: ἱκάνω — come to, reach, arrive at; pres. 1 sg. mid. (deponent form ἱκάνομαι): ’I come to (your knees)’
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον) · also aor. 3 pl. (the same ending serves both persons): ’they saw’
ἴμεν: εἶμι — go; pres. inf., epic (= Attic ἰέναι)
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative
ἵν: ἵνα — so that, in order that; conj., elided (ἵν’ = ἵνα)
ὀδυσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. nom. sg., single-σ metrical variant Ὀδυσεύς
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδυσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; acc. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆα)
ὀιζυρὸν: ὀιζυρός — wretched, full of misery; masc. acc. sg., predicative: ’(bore him) to be wretched’
ὀνόμαζεν: ὀνομάζω — call by name, name; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ὠνόμαζε); with ἐκ in tmesis (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζεν) ’called by name’
ὀξὺ: ὀξύς — sharp, keen; neut. acc. sg.
ὀπωπῆς: ὀπωπή — sight, act of seeing; fem. gen. sg.
ὀφθαλμοῖσι: ὀφθαλμός — eye; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οῖς)
ὀφθαλμοῖσιν: ὀφθαλμός — eye; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν)
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλεθρον: ὄλεθρος — destruction, ruin, death; acc. sg.
ὄπωπας: ὁράω — see; perf. 2 sg.: ’you have seen’
ὄρχαμε: ὄρχαμος — chief, leader (etymology uncertain); masc. voc. sg.: ’chief’ (ὄρχαμε λαῶν, variant of ὄρχαμος ἀνδρῶν)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅπως: ὅπως — so that, in order that, how; + subj. or fut. indic. · also + opt., in secondary sequence after a past-tense verb, indirect deliberative: ’how it might’ (ὅπως ἄριστα γένοιτο ’how it might turn out best’) · also ’when’ = ὅτε
ὅσσοι: ὅσος — as much/many as; epic ὅσσος, masc. nom. pl.: ’as many as’ (correlative with τόσσοι)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’
ὑπέρβιον: ὑπέρβιος — overweening, excessive; fem./neut. acc. sg.
ὑποστὰς: ὑφίστημι — place under; intr. (aor. 2 act. and mid.) undertake, promise; aor. 2 part. act. masc. nom. sg., intr.: ’having promised’
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’)
ὑψηλοῖο: ὑψηλός — high, lofty; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὕβριν: ὕβρις — insolence, wanton violence; fem. acc. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὤρνυτ: ὄρνυμι — stir, rouse; impf. mid. 3 sg., elided (ὤρνυτ’ = ὤρνυτο): ’rose’
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥήγεα: ῥῆγος — rug, coverlet (laid on a bed); neut. nom./acc. pl.
ῥοδοδάκτυλος: ῥοδοδάκτυλος — rose-fingered; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
